title: Smart prefetch rollout with siloed approval for Optimize suggestions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Optimize suggestions (batching/caching configs) are high-value for cost but risky to apply broadly. Current autopilot flows either require full manual approval or apply too aggressively, causing latency regressions or inference errors in edge cases.

Goal: Implement a safe, automated pathway that prefetches candidate config changes, evaluates them with lightweight noninvasive techniques (shadow and synthetic replay), and exposes a siloed approval flow in Console so teams can opt-in, sign-off, or reject. This ticket covers the rollout orchestration, approval gating, canary policy expressor, and the rollback playbook.

Success metrics: reduction in time-to-adopt validated cost recs by 40% for pilot customers; <=0.5% incidence of customer-visible latency/regression after rollout; ability to fully revert a config within 5 minutes after detection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Candidate configs are prefetched and staged in a 'pending' state in the config store.
- A preflight simulation (synthetic replay of representative prompt traces) runs automatically and produces pass/fail verdicts with per-metric deltas.
- Shadow traffic experiment returns resource and latency deltas under production load without modifying customer outputs.
- Console shows a Silo Approval UI where: workspace admins, platform owners, and security can each approve independently.
- Rollout controller supports linear ramps (0->1%->5%->25%->100%) with metric gates at each step.
- Automatic abort/rollback triggers on any gate breach and executes an observable rollback job.
- End-to-end integration tests and a canary in staging are green.
implementation_notes:
Architecture components:
1) Prefetcher service: pulls Optimize suggestions and compiles candidate server configs into a staging namespace. Adds metadata (origin, suggested_by, expected_cost_delta).
2) Preflight runner: uses lightweight synthetic replay harness and sample traces from Console-managed prompt sets. Reports CPU/GPU utilization delta, p50/p95 latency, and token-level error rates.
3) Shadow harness: routes a sampled percentage of real traffic to a shadow fleet with candidate config for noninvasive telemetry.
4) Rollout controller: state machine that executes ramp steps and evaluates policy gates via our telemetry engine.
5) Siloed Approval UI: Console component that surfaces approvals per-role and enforces approval requirements defined in a small DSL.
6) Reconciler + Revert: automated job that can revert candidate configs and apply whitelisted fallback variants.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Prefetching uses extra storage and ephemeral VMs for simulation; we limit size and TTL to reduce cost.
- Shadow experiments can increase load on serving clusters; we cap sample rates and prefer synthetic replay for very latency-sensitive customers.
- Approval complexity: we favor role-based approval (workspace-admin, platform-owner, security) with a simple required_approvals integer to avoid combinatorial policy matrices.

Policy DSL example (human-readable string saved in metadata):
"""canary_policy:
  steps:
    - pct: 1
      min_duration: 2m
      gates:
        - metric: p95_latency
          threshold: +10%
        - metric: error_rate
          threshold: +0.1%
    - pct: 10
      min_duration: 10m
      gates:
        - metric: p95_latency
          threshold: +5%
  required_approvals: [workspace-admin, platform-owner]
  allow_automatic_abort: true
"""
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): deploy prefetched configs to staging shadow cluster and run synthetic replay for 48h.
Phase 2 (pilot): select 3 pilot customers (low-latency, medium-latency, high-throughput) with opt-in flag. Run 1% shadow + 5% synthetic replay for 24h. Engineering on-call watches.
Phase 3 (canary ramp): if pilot signals OK, start linear ramp for opt-in customers per policy DSL (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Each step requires policy gates to pass and required approvals.
Phase 4 (wide): after 24h of stable metrics at 100% for pilot cohort, expand to other opt-in customers. Auto-apply only for customers with explicit opt-in or those in managed Optimize Dedicated contracts.
tests:
- Unit tests for Prefetcher: config serialization, TTL eviction.
- Integration test: preflight runner produces deterministic deltas for known traces.
- E2E: staging canary job runs simulated ramp and aborts on injected regressions.
- Chaos test: simulate one serving node OOM during ramp to validate rollback and fallback variant.
- Load test: shadow harness at 2x normal sample rate to ensure no resource exhaustion.
- Manual test checklist for pilot onboarding (Console opt-in flow, RBAC checks, notification hooks).
monitoring_playbook:
- Primary metrics to watch: p50/p95 latency, error_rate (5xx), GPU_util, tokens_per_second, tail_qps, cost_per_100k_tokens.
- Gates: any metric breach beyond thresholds in policy DSL triggers an automatic pause and notifies oncall.
- Runbook steps: 1) Verify telemetry integrity (no missing shards). 2) If breach confirmed, hit 'Abort' in Console to trigger rollback job. 3) If rollback fails, escalate to infra with priority 'paged'. 4) Postmortem: tag incident with ENG- and link to improve preflight coverage.
- Alerting: create composite alert that triggers if (policy_gate_breaches > 0) AND (time_since_ramp_start < 2h).
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Kapoor): Love the preflight approach; ask that we expose expected cost savings in the Console card before approval.

Design (Leah Kim): Siloed approvals need clearer affordances for 'conditional approvals' (approve if staging metrics show <3% cost regression). We'll iterate UI copy and add inline telemetry snapshots.
Security (Olivia Chen): Ensure the prefetched configs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled. Marked security_review_required=true.
Infra (Tomás Ruiz): Shadow experiments will add load; propose a global shadow_shaper to throttle shadow traffic per-region.
